about: Transcript Markdown as the web console reads it (md() in ui/src/model/markdown.ts), the reference for both phones: docs/session-liveness.md, 'Client presentation policy'; decision F in docs/web-console-carbon.md; SE-C90 to SE-C104 in docs/web-console-contracts.md.

Read by ui/src/model/shared-fixtures.spec.ts, ios/AgentRouter/Tests/SharedFixtureTests.swift and android/app/src/test/java/ca/whnet/agentrouter/SharedFixtureTest.kt. Each maps its own client's blocks to the shape below and compares them with `expected`.

`expected` is generated from the web's model, never written by hand: edit a case's name, input or pending, then in ui/ run `UPDATE_SHARED_FIXTURES=1 pnpm exec vitest run src/model/shared-fixtures.spec.ts`.

`pending` marks a case the clients disagree on where a phone would lose information by matching the web. Every suite skips it, by name, until it is decided; `expected` still records what the web does.
{type: paragraph, runs}: one line of prose, its whitespace at the start kept.
{type: heading, level, runs}: level is the level the web draws, # as 3, ## as 4, ### as 5, and deeper as 6.
{type: list, ordered, items}: one run list per item; ordered is whether the items are drawn numbered.
{type: code, lang, text}: text is verbatim; lang is the fence's language tag, null when the client drops it, as every client does today.
{type: table, head, rows}: head is a list of cells, rows a list of rows of cells, and a cell is a list of runs.

Runs are the inline formatting of a line, an item or a cell, flattened: {text}, with bold, italic and code present and true when they apply, and href when the text is a link. Adjacent runs with the same styles are merged, and empty runs are left out.
